pull.title: KAFKA-21234: FileRecords#readInto should honor slice boundaries (#23737)
pull.body:
Cherry-pick of #23737 to the `3.9` branch.

When the metadata layer (e.g. `MetadataLoader`) reads a slice of records from KRaft that is larger than `KafkaRaftClient#MAX_BATCH_SIZE_BYTES`, `RecordsIterator` can return records past the end of the slice (the HWM). `FileRecords#readInto` reads up to the end of the underlying file instead of the end of the `FileRecords` slice, which can lead to a metadata error where the node tries to snapshot with records past the HWM.

This change bounds `FileRecords#readInto` to the end of the `FileRecords` object, so reading a `[start position, HWM)` slice never reads bytes past the HWM into memory. `RecordsIterator` also stops growing its buffer once it has read the whole slice, since a trailing partial batch can't be completed.

Original PR: https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23737

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Reviewers: Chia-Ping Tsai <chia7712@gmail.com>

issue_comments.body:
Notes for reviewers:

The `FileRecords#readInto` change applies as on trunk. Differences from the trunk commit:

- `RecordsIterator`: 3.9 has no `firstBatchSize` local or "Creating a new buffer" log line, so only the new condition is applied.
- `RecordsIteratorTest`: kept this branch's jqwik `@Property` tests, as in the 4.2 and 4.3 backports. The new `createIterator(records, bufferSupplier, batchSize, validateCrc)` overload uses the 3.9 constructor, which takes a `RecordSerde` and no `LogContext`.
- 3.9 compiles tests with `--release 8`, so `List.of`/`Set.of` became `Arrays.asList`, `Collections.singletonList` and `Collections.emptySet`.
- `MemoryRecords#slice` doesn't exist on 3.9, so `testRecordsEndingInPartialBatch` builds the partial `MemoryRecords` from a duplicate of the buffer with a lower limit.
- `FileRecordsTest`: added the `ParameterizedTest`/`ValueSource` imports, and `testReadIntoWithPositionOutsideRecords` declares `throws IOException` because `FileRecords#slice` throws it on 3.9.
- Ran locally on JDK 17: `./gradlew :clients:test --tests 'org.apache.kafka.common.record.*' :raft:test`, plus `checkstyleMain`, `checkstyleTest` and `spotlessCheck` for `clients` and `raft`. All passed.

commit.message:
KAFKA-21234: FileRecords#readInto should honor slice boundaries (#23737)

When the metadata layer (e.g. MetadataLoader) tries to read a slice of
records from KRaft which is greater than
KafkaRaftClient#MAX_BATCH_SIZE_BYTES, the RecordsIterator can return
records which are past the slice (HWM). As it iterates through this
slice of
records, FileRecords#readInto reads from disk the minimum of the bytes
until end of the file and the remaining space in the associated buffer.
In the case of the former, this can lead to a metadata error where the
node tries to snapshot with records past the HWM.

For the metadata error to occur, the following three pre-conditions must
be met:

1. One committed read handed to a listener is larger than 8 MiB.
2. The segment file has bytes after the HWM, meaning records this node
already appended but that aren't committed yet.
3. For the error to actually show up, the snapshot generator emits a
snapshot from the resulting image before the HWM catches up.

The underlying cause is the same as KAFKA-20841. Thanks to @asdf2014
for working on this issue as part of
https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/22963.

Change `FileRecords#readInto` which reads from the underlying file to
the minimum of:

1. The remaining space in the associated buffer, which in the case of
RecordsIterator is the minimum of the FileRecords' record size and
the batch size defined by KRaft.
2. The end byte position of the FileRecords object, rather than the end
of the underlying file. This ensures when a caller constructs a
FileRecords slice of [start position, HWM), no bytes past the HWM are
read into memory.

Co-authored-by: Benedict Jin <asdf2014@apache.org>
Reviewers: José Armando García Sancio <jsancio@apache.org>, Jun Rao
<junrao@gmail.com>, Zhiyan Tang <ztang@confluent.io>, Chia-Ping Tsai
<chia7712@gmail.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
